metadata.provenance: All scenarios are authored synthetic examples. No real message, person, brand, domain or phone number is used; URLs use reserved .test/.example hosts or documentation IP ranges.
metadata.drafted_by: Drafted with Claude (AI assistant) for @devisripriyanam. Labels have not been reviewed by two teammates.
metadata.label_policy: expected_verdict is the label a careful human reader would assign from the supplied text alone: suspected_scam needs a deceptive pressure, impersonation, or request for a secret or payment; spam is unsolicited promotion; legitimate is an expected notice or ordinary message with no such request; unknown means the supplied evidence is not enough. It is not the output of any detector.
metadata.purpose: 20 held-out scenarios. Run only for the final measurement; never tune on them.

scenarios.support: Travel notification that asks for nothing

input.text: Your March statement is ready in the app. We will never ask for your PIN by message.

input.text: Work-from-home data entry: pay a $75 registration fee at http://198.51.100.77/register to access tasks.

scenarios.support: Job lure that charges a registration fee at an IP-address host
Punycode host with a login path; could be a legitimate internationalised domain, so reviewers must confirm.

messages.text: I want the bike. This is urgent, I leave tonight.
Great, when can you collect it?
First confirm the verification code I just sent you.

scenarios.support: Buyer pairs urgency with a request for a verification code; only the buyer's messages count

messages.text: Urgent reminder: never send your OTP to anyone who asks.

scenarios.support: Urgency and OTP wording appear only in the protected user's own message, which must be excluded
Blank-only input is not a meaningful request and must be rejected, not analysed

input.text: Final reminder: settle your overdue invoice today at http://198.51.100.99/invoice

scenarios.support: Text check misses the overall deadline; the completed URL result must be preserved
